item.title: Lindsay Clancy mistrial declared after jury deadlocks in killings of her three children
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial centered on whether severe mental illness relieved her of criminal responsibility in the January 2023 deaths of her three children.
item.content:encoded:
Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Friday in Lindsay Clancy’s murder case after jurors said they were unable to reach a unanimous verdict in the killings of her three children after a week of deliberating at the Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts.

The mistrial followed a dramatic dispute over an alleged 11-1 divide, with Clancy’s defense arguing that the lone holdout juror had acknowledged doubt but was refusing to properly apply the court’s instructions on reasonable doubt.

The alleged holdout is believed to be one of the three male jurors on the 12-person panel after defense attorney Kevin Reddington repeatedly referred to the unnamed juror as "he" in court.

Clancy’s attorneys made an emergency appeal to the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court in an attempt to stay the mistrial and force further inquiry into the juror. Justice Dalila Argaez Wendlandt denied the request Friday afternoon, clearing the way for Sullivan to formally declare the mistrial.

POSTPARTUM MOM LINDSAY CLANCY ON TRIAL FOR MURDER BRINGS COURT TO A HALT WITH SUDDEN BREAKDOWN

HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

Clancy had been charged with first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths of her children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. Each of the children had been strangled with exercise bands.

The trial centered on whether she was legally responsible for her actions at the time, and the defense argued she wasn't due to postpartum psychosis.

Her attorneys argued that severe mental illness left her unable to appreciate the wrongfulness of what she was doing or unable to conform her conduct to the requirements of the law.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN

Prosecutors maintained that Clancy remained criminally responsible and pointed to evidence they said showed planning, purposeful behavior and an awareness of what she was doing before, during and after the killings.

During the trial, Clancy's former husband, Patrick Clancy, testified about the day of the slayings, which happened while he was running errands that included picking up children's stool softener at a CVS store and takeout for dinner. They spoke on the phone while he was out.

Under Massachusetts law, once lack of criminal responsibility is properly raised, prosecutors must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that a defendant was criminally responsible.

The mistrial means the case ended without a verdict and Clancy was neither convicted nor acquitted. Prosecutors can seek to retry her but have not yet announced a decision.

Sullivan said he wants the case retried "sooner rather than later," suggesting a new trial could potentially take place later this fall. Clancy is due back in court Sept. 29 for a status hearing, trial assignment and a defense Rule 25 motion.

All previous bail orders remain in effect.

JUDGE SENTENCES NEVADA MOM FOR DROWNING YOUNG SON, DAUGHTER: 'I WILL REMEMBER YOUR CASE FOREVER'

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

The mistrial followed a trial that focused extensively on Clancy's psychiatric condition in the months and weeks before the children died.

Jurors heard testimony about her treatment by mental-health professionals, psychiatric medications, anxiety, depression, insomnia and other symptoms documented before the killings.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

On Jan. 24, 2023, authorities responded to the Clancy family's Duxbury home after Patrick Clancy returned and found his wife seriously injured outside the house.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

The couple's three children were found inside.

BROOKLYN MOTHER WHO DROWNED HER THREE CHILDREN IN THE OCEAN NEAR CONEY ISLAND SENTENCED TO DECADES IN PRISON

Cora and Dawson died that night. Callan was taken to a hospital and died several days later.

Lindsay Clancy survived after jumping from a second-story window and suffered injuries that left her paralyzed in a wheelchair.

The prosecution and defense offered sharply different explanations for what happened before the children were killed.

The defense had argued that the deaths occurred after months of worsening psychiatric symptoms and treatment and that Clancy's mental condition had deteriorated to the point that she could not legally be held criminally responsible.

Specifically, the defense contended that Clancy heard a male voice that commanded her to kill her three children. Dr. Phillip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist, said it was almost as if she was a "puppet."

SEND US A TIP

"Not only did she hear a command, but she felt that her body was taken over by an external force where she was in a dream state and did not have control of her own body. It was almost like she was a puppet and someone else was pulling the strings," Resnick said.

However, prosecutors rejected that claim and their experts argued that Clancy deliberately created an opportunity to be alone with the children and intentionally killed them.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Gregory Saathoff, a forensic psychiatrist at the University of Virginia who consults for the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit, told jurors that Clancy's self-described auditory hallucinations were "very unusual."

"What was significant to me is that she had not spoken about hearing voices before to any of the mental health professionals, psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, physicians and staff in the emergency department, or at McLean," Saathoff said.

"This was the first time she reported that, and that she experienced an auditory hallucination, according to what she told me. So that was unusual. And then what was very unusual was the fact that the voice stopped with the strangling of her youngest son," he added.

During the trial, members of Clancy's family revealed they were "very concerned" about her mental health in the months before she killed her three kids.

Susan Clancy, Lindsay's mother-in-law, told jurors she was concerned about her mental health during the holiday season in 2022, but said she was a caring mother.

"Lindsay was struggling. We were all very concerned," Susan Clancy said. "She was very nurturing, very loving. She was a wonderful mother. Wonderful."

"She was begging for help," Susan Clancy said.

Paula Musgrove, Lindsay Clancy's mother, also told jurors about the mental health problems. In an Oct. 20, 2022 text message, Lindsay Clancy asked her mother for help.

"Mom, will you please come up and stay with me for a bit? I'm really sick. Something is wrong. I had horrible insomnia all night, and I just don’t know how I am going to get through the day... It’s just really scary, and I don’t want to be alone," the text read.

item.title: West Virginia principal suspended after recording devices found in girls’ locker rooms
item.description: The Brooke County principal faces two felony charges and is being held on $100,000 bond after officials reportedly found devices at the school and his home.
item.content:encoded:
School administrators immediately suspended a West Virginia high school principal Wednesday after officials reportedly discovered recording devices placed in multiple locker rooms.

The criminal investigation involves Eric James, 53, who served as principal of Brooke High School in Wellsburg.

Officials said four devices were found in the female physical education locker rooms, including a separate locker room and another dressing area used by the school's dance team, according to WTOV 9.

"Yesterday, after students were released, Brooke County Schools was informed of a criminal investigation into allegations that a recording device was placed in a locker room at Brooke High School," a Thursday memo from the school system said, according to Lede News.

LOUDOUN COUNTY HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT ACCUSED OF FILMING STUDENTS IN BATHROOM UNDER INVESTIGATION

The devices were removed from campus with the help of school security officers, staff and law enforcement, according to reports.

Additional devices were reportedly confiscated at James' home, officials said.

James is being held at the Northern Regional Jail in Marshall County, West Virginia, on $100,000 bond, according to the state Magistrate Database and the West Virginia Regional Jail Authority.

FLORIDA MAN ALLEGEDLY RECORDED GIRLS IN CHURCH BATHROOM WITH HIDDEN CAMERA, ARRESTED ON VOYEURISM CHARGES

He was charged Thursday with two felony counts, including one count of intentionally intercepting or attempting to intercept wire, oral or electronic communications and one count of breaking and entering a nonresidence.

The school system said it "will be meeting with students, parents, and staff to offer supportive measures while the investigations continue," according to Lede News.

"The safety, security, and privacy of our students are fundamental responsibilities of our school system. Conduct that compromises those responsibilities will not be tolerated. The school system is cooperating fully with law enforcement and is also conducting its own investigations into the matter," the school said.

item.title: Ocasio-Cortez calls focus on Hasan Piker 'absolutely ludicrous' as some Democrats demand distance
item.description: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez called it "ludicrous" that Congress is focused on Twitch streamer Hasan Piker as Democrats debate his political influence.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., brushed off far-left streamer Hasan Piker's role in American politics on Thursday, questioning why people were focused or devoting time to him.

"It is absolutely ludicrous that so much oxygen from sitting elected officials in the United States Congress is being dedicated to discourse around a Twitch streamer for young people," Ocasio-Cortez, a member of the progressive Squad, said according to The Hill.

Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., also didn't dismiss him outright, telling the outlet she wouldn't defend all his views.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT DEMANDS REPORTERS STOP ASKING 'ABOUT HASAN PIKER' AHEAD OF SENATE RACE

"That's for him to do," Jayapal said.

"I don’t know why, all of a sudden, the standard is you have to agree with everything he said."

HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS

Jaypal told the outlet Democrats needed to reach Piker's voters.

"I think that we have been talking about how we need to reach out to all parts of our party and also how difficult it is sometimes to get people to pay attention to politics, and, so, streamers are important in that," Jayapal said.

The Hill cited multiple Democrats who have dismissed Piker, including Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., who told the outlet, "Not only should people not be on stage with him or take his support, they should condemn his views and what he has said.

"And I think anything short of that is unacceptable."

SOME DEMOCRATS PRIVATELY DISGUSTED BY HASAN PIKER BUT ARE AFRAID TO PUBLICLY CRITICIZE HIM, HOUSE DEM CLAIMS

Piker has campaigned with several Democrats this midterm election cycle, including Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for Senate in Michigan. Other Democrats have expressed the importance of reaching Piker's listeners, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.

Sanders was asked about Piker's past statements on 9/11, which the streamer has since walked back. 

Sanders condemned the comments and told CNN in August, "He has a whole lot of followers and a lot of things that he's saying that are making sense to a lot of people. I think, you know, we have to get above cancel culture. You know, when you're doing radio, whatever they do, podcasts three hours a day, you say dumb things."

ABDUL EL-SAYED PLAYS DOWN HASAN PIKER TIES AFTER STREAMER’S VIRAL ANTISEMITISM FIRESTORM

Speaking to Stephen A. Smith during his show, "Straight Shooter," El-Sayed said this week he was trying to reach Piker's listeners.

"What I'm saying is there are 3 million people who listen to Hasan," El-Sayed said. "I want to offer them a pathway into an electoral movement where, rather than sit outside of the electoral system, they see a pathway around the things that they agree with that he says that I agree with and a pathway that disavows the things that I disagree with. And, so, it's important."

Smith summarized El-Sayed's strategy as an effort to win over Piker's audience rather than an endorsement of the streamer personally.

"So, you're not thinking about him. You’re not thinking about him. You’re thinking about the 3 million people that support him, and you're trying to get those votes. That's what you're saying?" Smith said.

DEM CANDIDATE ERUPTS IN PROFANE DEFENSE OF HASAN PIKER AS PARTY FIGURES DISTANCE THEMSELVES

"Exactly," El-Sayed said.

Fox News Digital reported last week that El-Sayed attempted to put distance between his campaign and Piker after the streamer faced backlash over comments about American Jews and Israel. Piker endorsed El-Sayed and appeared at multiple campaign events, including his primary night gathering.

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital in a statement, "A lot of these folks are being rather disingenuous. Yes, media is running wild, arguably disproportionately so, with this Piker story, but a big reason for that is El-Sayed’s hard to understand refusal to create more distance between himself and the streamer or just flat disavow him.

"You can’t have it both ways. Either he is just some random streamer or he is a critical figure for the left’s political movement. His refusal to … denounce him suggests the latter, though strategically it seems Piker is more of a liability than a help. Recent polling showed the vast majority of Democrats don’t like him."

Schroff said Democrats like him have been consistent in calling out President Donald Trump for "dining with Nick Fuentes and bringing Laura Loomer into his inner circle."

"And the reason certain candidates do have the burden to disavow Piker is not because he is some influencer who boosts them. … They have actively sought him out, campaigned with him and joined his streaming platform," he added. "Normal Democrats do not want to be associated with the insane things Piker has said."

"AOC, Bernie Sanders and Abdul El-Sayed rolled out the red carpet for Hasan Piker, but now that voters are catching on to how insane his views are, they've developed a sudden case of amnesia," RNC spokesman Max Lippel told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"Piker has always been an America-hating extremist, and if they didn't want to answer for his disgusting views, they should have never requested he campaign with them to begin with."

The account then followed up with a post calling Piker "our Twitch streamer."

Fox News' CJ Womack contributed to this report.

item.title: Americans headed for high-risk nation urged to prepare wills, leave DNA samples ahead of time
item.description: The State Department's Libya travel advisory warns of kidnapping, terrorism and landmines. It also urges Americans to write a will and leave DNA samples with doctors.
item.content:encoded:
Americans who may be planning a trip to Libya are being urged to reconsider those plans, as the U.S. State Department has issued its strongest possible travel warning.

The department recently updated Libya's Level 4 "Do Not Travel" advisory, warning Americans not to visit the country for any reason due to crime, terrorism, health concerns, unrest, kidnapping and landmines. The overall advisory level did not change.

"Do not travel to Libya for any reason," the advisory states.

AMERICANS WARNED OF KIDNAPPING, EXTORTION AS VIOLENT CRIME GRIPS PARTS OF TOURIST SPOT

The State Department warns that clashes between armed groups and government-aligned forces can break out at any time — while weapons are widespread throughout the country.

"Prepare a will and end-of-life instructions," the advisory states. Travelers are also advised to designate insurance beneficiaries or draft a power of attorney.

Criminal organizations are known to be involved in drug and human trafficking and other smuggling activity, while targeted kidnappings and assassinations are common, according to the advisory.

"Kidnapping is widespread, and victims have included U.S. citizens," officials warn.

Americans could also have limited options for help in an emergency.

"There is currently no U.S. Embassy in Libya," the advisory states. 

It added that the U.S. government cannot provide emergency services to Americans in the country because of the security risks.

The State Department also warns that terrorist attacks could occur with little or no warning, while demonstrations can turn violent and disrupt transportation and other essential services.

Landmines and unexploded ordnance pose another danger throughout the North African country, with officials warning that their locations are often unmarked or difficult to recognize.

Travelers are advised to avoid roadside ditches, shoulders and unmarked trails and never touch anything that could be unexploded munitions.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

For Americans who decide to travel to Libya despite the warning, the State Department recommends having a plan to leave in an emergency that does not depend on U.S. government assistance.

Officials also advise travelers to share important documents and login information with loved ones, develop a communication plan and consider hiring a professional security organization.

The State Department further recommends establishing a "proof of life protocol" with loved ones in case a traveler is taken hostage.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Leave DNA samples with your medical provider in case it is necessary for your family to access them for identification purposes," the advisory states.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for further details.

The warning comes as U.S. officials continue issuing travel and security advisories for destinations around the world.

Fox News Digital recently reported that Americans who are planning to travel to Israel are urged to reconsider their plans due to terrorism and unrest, with certain areas carrying the highest Level 4 "Do Not Travel" warning.

Those areas include locations near the Gaza Strip, the Israel-Egypt border and parts of northern Israel due to armed conflict.

item.title: ‘Fiesta Mexicana’: El-Sayed campaign plans festive 9/11 while remembrance is missing from public schedule
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's campaign scheduled county fair and Fiesta Mexicana events on 9/11's 25th anniversary, raising questions about the Michigan Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
While Americans prepare to mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, Abdul El-Sayed’s public campaign schedule for that day makes no mention of a remembrance event, but includes a Mexican festival, a farmers market and a county fair.

As of Friday morning, El-Sayed’s campaign website listed staff and volunteers for Grand Rapids’ Fiesta Mexicana, a nearby farmers market and the Allegan County Fair, while El-Sayed himself was scheduled to make a stop on his "Shouldn’t Be This Hard" tour.

After Fox News Digital asked about the lack of a 9/11 remembrance on the public schedule, El-Sayed’s campaign said the Democrat nominee "will be attending a 9/11 remembrance memorial event that day," though the event was not listed on his campaign website.

FOX NEWS MEDIA ANNOUNCES EXTENSIVE 9/11 ANNIVERSARY COVERAGE FROM GROUND ZERO, PENTAGON AND SHANKSVILLE

The events listed on the campaign schedule have a notably more festive tone.

Fiesta Mexicana, for instance, describes itself as "three days of mariachi, folklórico and forty-some vendors" that uses "music, food, dance and good company" to "make sure Mexican culture is known, understood and celebrated in West Michigan — on our own terms." El-Sayed’s campaign instructs supporters to "bring some Mexican swag" and "go inside to enjoy the music and get some food."

The Allegan County Fair, meanwhile, features live entertainment, food, games and rides.

El-Sayed’s campaign pointed out, that of the four events flagged by Fox News Digital — Fiesta Mexicana, the farmers market, the county fair and the candidate’s tour event — the Senate candidate would not be attending two of them, though would not specify which ones.

The campaign did not explain why El-Sayed's website did not list the 9/11 remembrance memorial event on his list of upcoming events, but it did underscore in a comment to Fox News Digital that El-Sayed views 9/11 as a horrific moment in history.

"The September 11th terrorist attacks were an evil attack on America's freedom and he will be joining Michiganders in remembering the 25th anniversary," El-Sayed’s spokeswoman told Fox News Digital.

BIDEN-WORLD VETERAN ISSUES STARK WARNING ABOUT ABDUL EL-SAYED AS HE CROSSES PARTY LINES

The Michigan Senate hopeful has a complicated relationship with 9/11.

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, whom El-Sayed had campaigned alongside, caused him a headache early in the campaign when a clip of the streamer saying that America "deserved 9/11" resurfaced. El-Sayed called the statement "dumb," though did not disavow Piker.

Later, old blogs and social media posts where El-Sayed made controversial statements about the terrorist attacks began to surface.

SANDERS-BACKED DEM BLISTERED FOR MAKING 'EXCUSES FOR TERRORISTS,' SLAMMING 'HIGH AND MIGHTY' AMERICANS

Fox News Digital previously reported that El-Sayed equated 9/11 with Jan. 6 and President Donald Trump with Osama bin Laden on a now private blog. In social media posts, he called on Americans to bring the same outrage to the COVID-19 pandemic that they felt for 9/11 and mourned the deaths of those killed in America’s War on Terror.

item.title: Scientists discover new tick-borne virus after testing thousands of patients with mysterious illnesses
item.description: The Asian longhorned tick nairovirus caused flu-like illness and thrombocytopenia in over 10% of tick-bitten patients studied in a China lab.
item.content:encoded:
Scientists in China have identified a previously unknown tick-borne virus that can cause flu-like illness, fatigue and gastrointestinal symptoms, according to a new study.

The newly discovered virus, the Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), which is part of the orthonairovirus group, has also been found to cause thrombocytopenia (reduced blood platelet counts) and laboratory evidence of liver-cell injury or inflammation.

Since 2009, Chinese researchers have been tracking patients with unusual illnesses, including severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), according to Dr. Sharon Nachman, chief of pediatric infectious diseases at Stony Brook Children’s Hospital in New York.

NO CURE, NO VACCINE: EXPERTS WARN OF RARE BOURBON VIRUS AFTER FIRST NY CASE

"Thrombocytopenia is low platelet count, so those patients bled, and it had about a 30% mortality, which is quite high," she told Fox News Digital. "So, they kept following those patients."

Many of the cases were linked to Dabie bandavirus (DBV), a tick-borne hemorrhagic fever, but it was not the most common virus.

After extensive testing of blood samples and viral fragments, researchers identified the new virus, ALTNV, which is genetically distinct from DBV.

Researchers from the State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity in Beijing identified the virus in 10.4% of 3,163 patients who had been bitten by ticks.

HANTAVIRUS IN THE US: WHERE THE RARE, SOMETIMES DEADLY DISEASE HAS BEEN FOUND

Patients who had both ALTNV and DBV were more likely to have respiratory issues and kidney complications. Seven (18.4%) of these patients died during the course of the study.

"The cocirculation of ALTNV and DBV in the same areas, coupled with their shared tick vector, underscores the need for improved differential diagnosis between infections with these viruses in regions where SFTS is endemic," the authors concluded.

The findings were published this week in the New England Journal of Medicine.

"The big picture is that ticks carry lots of viruses," Nachman said. "We're getting smarter at identifying those viruses. And when one blood sample is negative, it's important to say, 'Maybe there was a new virus there, and let's look for it.'"

Illness from ALTNV can initially resemble the flu, causing fever, muscle aches, fatigue and sometimes respiratory symptoms.

Although an ALTNV infection can cause low platelet counts, the study did not link the virus alone to severe bleeding or deaths. The fatal cases involved patients who were also infected with DBV, which causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome.

Because tick-borne viral symptoms can overlap with many infections, Nachman emphasized the importance of identifying the specific virus.

"Effective antivirals exist for flu, but not for many tick-borne viruses, including the newly identified one," she said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

For most patients, supportive care is given to help manage symptoms, "but it's also about being smart and not giving patients the wrong medication," Nachman noted. "And we certainly don't want to use antibiotics because those only work for bacteria, not for viruses."

Nachman shared the best practices she recommends to families looking to avoid tick bites.

"Wear the right clothing, meaning long pants, tucking them into your socks, and use tick repellents on your skin if you're an adult or on your clothing if you're a young child," she advised.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

It’s also important to be on the lookout for ticks on the skin.

"The longer the tick is on your skin, the more it's engorged, the more it’s likely to pass an infection to you," Nachman said. "So, removing them after you've gone hiking or walking on the beach will be really important."

While the Asian longhorn tick is not yet seen in the U.S., Nachman noted there are "lots and lots of other ticks, and those ticks carry other diseases."

"I don't want to say one tick is worse than another tick. It's rather all about the diseases they carry and who you are," she said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"So, if you're a healthy adult, and you get babesiosis, you often get better without any medications. But if you're an immune-compromised adult, you're going to be quite sick.

"It’s not really about the ticks. It’s about the patient. Who are you? What's your underlying illness if you have any? How old are you, and how healthy are you?"

item.title: Comer indicates McConnell staffers aiming for lawmaker to return to Senate later this month
item.description: Rep. James Comer indicated that he has spoken with McConnell staffers who indicated they are aiming for the senator will return later this month.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., indicated on Thursday that he has been in contact Sen. Mitch McConnell's, R-Ky., staff, who have indicated that the aim is for the lawmaker to return to the Senate later this month.

"I expect that. I sure hope so," Comer said after being asked if McConnell was expected to join his Senate colleagues on Sept. 14.

Comer said he had talked to McConnell staff, who have "said it’s their goal for senator McConnell to be here… when the Senate" returns.

MCCONNELL IS OUT OF REHAB, BUT HIS ABSENCE HAS STUNTED A KEY REPUBLICAN PRIORITY

Fox News Digital reached out to McConnell's office on Friday.

Senators are slated to return to work in Washington, D.C., on Sept. 14.

"Other than pro forma sessions on Tuesday September 8th at 1:15 p.m. and Thursday September 10th at 3:00 p.m. the Senate stands adjourned until 3:00 p.m. on Monday, September 14th. There is one vote that evening at 5:30 p.m.," according to the U.S. Senate Press Gallery website.

KENTUCKY GOVERNOR CALLS ON MCCONNELL TO PROVE HE IS FIT TO SERVE OR RESIGN: 'ADDRESS THE PEOPLE'

McConnell, 84, suffered a fall in June.

In a statement nearly a month ago, the lawmaker noted that he had been released from a rehabilitation center.

SEN MITCH MCCONNELL HOSPITALIZED, 'RECEIVING EXCELLENT CARE,' HIS OFFICE SAYS

The lawmaker, who has served in the Senate since 1985, is not running for re-election this year.

item.title: Non-citizen police officers approved after Dem says ICE 'invasion' 'sends a message'
item.description: Danbury, Connecticut's city council voted 18-2 to let non-citizen immigrants and DACA recipients serve as police officers amid ongoing ICE raids.
item.content:encoded:
After a week of ICE raids, the Democrat-dominated City Council of Danbury, Connecticut, voted nearly unanimously to approve non-citizen legal residents serving as police officers.

Under the new guidance, approved in an 18-2 vote, non-citizen legal residents and Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients living in Danbury are allowed to serve as police officers in Danbury.

One city council member, Democrat Joe Britton, remarked that the vote "sends a message to our immigrant community at large that you are welcome in Danbury."

ICE operations in the area resulted in more than 60 arrests, according to local reports. The arrests prompted public outrage in the community, including from city officials such as Britton, who called the raids "frightening."

BORDER CZAR TOM HOMAN FIRES BACK AFTER DEMOCRAT CHRIS MURPHY CLAIMS ICE IS ‘TERRORIZING LITTLE KIDS’

The only two council members to vote against the measure were Republicans, while the council’s 17 Democrats and one Republican voted in favor.

Before the vote, Britton said that "what we have here is an opportunity." He noted that "though this definitely wasn’t planned to be on the agenda on the end of a federal invasion of immigration officials in Danbury … I do think it's timely."

"There is no reason to vote against this, and if you do vote against this, I truly question your moral compass," he added.

Britton emphasized that this change "is legal, it's allowed" and said it has been recommended.

Britton told Fox News Digital that "Danbury is an immigrant city, and I believe someone who is lawfully here, committed to our community, and willing to raise their hand and take an oath to protect and serve should have the opportunity to do so."

He added that "this change does not lower Danbury’s standards for becoming a police officer. It simply allows otherwise qualified lawful permanent residents and DACA recipients to apply and compete for these positions."

He noted that "every applicant must still satisfy the same training, background, character, and certification requirements required of any other officer," saying, "This was about expanding the pool of qualified applicants while maintaining the same high standards our residents expect from their police department."

Similarly, Taylor O'Brien, a spokesperson for the Danbury city government, told Fox News Digital that council "amended its ordinance in accordance with Connecticut's Police Officer Standards and Training Council, allowing legal permanent residents and DACA recipients to apply to become officers in the Danbury Police Department."

DEM SENATE NOMINEE CHANGES TUNE ON ICE AFTER VOWING NOT 'ONE MORE DIME' FOR AGENCY

O'Brien said that "this standard is followed by over 30 municipalities in Connecticut and several states across the country" and that it "opens Danbury's applicant pool to otherwise qualified candidates, including legal Danbury residents, who are currently applying to be police officers in other communities."

In 2020, the Connecticut Police Officer Standards and Training Council "partially waived" the citizenship requirement, extending eligibility for law enforcement candidates in Connecticut to lawful permanent residents and DACA recipients, according to the Connecticut Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection.

O'Brien added that Danbury Mayor Roberto Alves, a Democrat, "ensures Danbury maintains a rigorous hiring process for our Police Officers," adding that "this amendment should encourage qualified residents from the Danbury community to apply to serve the City they call home."

According to the Danbury News Times, Alves himself immigrated to the U.S. as an "undocumented child" and gained citizenship in 2017.

The outlet quoted Alves saying he is "glad the City Council approved" the measure. Alves emphasized that "the standards are not being lowered" and that "every applicant still has to meet the same rigorous background, training, fitness and professional standards required of any Danbury police officer."

"What we are doing is giving qualified people an opportunity to compete for the job," said Alves. "For a diverse city like Danbury, it strengthens our recruitment pool and gives us another opportunity to hire talented people who understand and care about the community they want to serve."

Fox News Digital reached out to Britton for additional comment.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Last year, ICE arrested two illegal immigrants who were serving as police officers. On July 25, 2025, Jamaican national Jon Luke Evans, who was serving as a reserve officer with the Old Orchard Beach, Maine, Police Department, was arrested on charges related to unlawfully attempting to purchase a gun. Then, on Oct. 15, Radule Bojovic, of Montenegro, who was serving as a police officer with the Hanover Park, Illinois, Police Department, was arrested during Operation Midway Blitz.

Fox News Digital's Sarah Rumpf-Whitten contributed to this report.

item.title: Former North Texas police officer given three life sentences for child pornography, solicitation of minor
item.description: A North Texas jury convicted Daniel Joseph Bates after he claimed 300-plus explicit child images were part of a secret human trafficking investigation.
item.content:encoded:
A former police officer in North Texas was ordered to serve three consecutive life sentences in prison after investigators found him in possession of over 300 videos and images of children being sexually abused, according to a statement from Johnson and Somerville Counties' district attorney.

Former Itasca Police Department Officer Daniel Joseph Bates was convicted Wednesday of possession of child pornography and online solicitation of a minor after a civilian set him up in an entrapment scheme, according to a statement District Attorney Timothy Good shared with Fox News Digital.

Texas Rangers arrested Bates after an adult decoy posing as a 15-year-old girl alerted police that Bates was communicating with someone he believed to be a minor, according to the statement.

The civilian alerted police to Bates' communications with him, prompting Rangers to obtain a search warrant for his digital devices, and they allegedly found over 300 images of minor children being sexually abused, according to the statement.

NEW MISSISSIPPI LAW EXPANDS DEATH PENALTY TO INCLUDE INMATES ON CHILD SEXUAL BATTERY CONVICTIONS

"The images and videos that had to be processed and presented to the jury are indescribable in the level of depravity they depict and the degree of deviance of the defendant who voluntarily possessed and viewed those types of images," Good said in the statement."

"Daniel Bates disgraced his badge and violated his oath and became the monster that he was sworn to protect the community from. Our community is safer with Bates serving three consecutive life sentences."

Bates testified that the child pornography in his possession was part of a secret investigation he was conducting into human traffickers, but prosecutors disputed that.

Bates was only a reserve police officer and, at the time of his arrest, was working highway construction security, according to authorities.

"Bates was unable to substantiate his claims that he was conducting an official police investigation," the statement read.

OHIO POLICE CHIEF ARRESTED IN FLORIDA AFTER GRAND JURY HANDS DOWN 70-COUNT CHILD SEX INDICTMENT

Bates reportedly told the person he was communicating with that, because he was a police officer, he carries a gun at all times. This prompted Arlind Queriman, a civilian who creates video content in which he exposes people who try to solicit minors for sex, to contact authorities, according to FOX 4 Dallas.

"Some people say we're vigilantes. Vigilantes beat up these people. I hand everything over to law enforcement," Queriman told FOX 4.

DRAG QUEEN SCHOOL BOARD VICE PRESIDENT ARRESTED ON CHILD PORNOGRAPHY AND ENDANGERMENT CHARGES

Bates also attempted to use his status as a reserve police officer to get out of the charges.

"He actually tried to play the badge thing," Good told FOX 4.

"The badge was supposed to be a shield for children — not a shield for a predator. He made his choices. The jury made its verdict. And the judge made sure his next choice will be made from a prison cell for the rest of his life," Assistant District Attorney Christy May said via the statement shared with Fox News Digital.

The three life sentences for child pornography possession are accompanied by a 40-year sentence for solicitation of a minor, according to the statement.

Fox News Digital contacted Itasca Police Department for further comment.

item.title: Women's cycling team manager speaks out after trans athlete competes against females in major competition
item.description: A trans athlete's late license upgrade before the Philadelphia Cycling Classic has team directors questioning USA Cycling's eligibility process.
item.content:encoded:
Nicola Cranmer, the general manager of the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) women's cycling team Virginia's Blue Ridge TWENTY28, provided a statement to OutKick after her riders recently competed in the Philadelphia Cycling Classic alongside a biological male trans athlete. The trans athlete did not finish.

Cranmer, who leads the longest running professional women's cycling team in the world, emphasized the importance of "protecting the integrity and fairness" in speaking out. 

"I have spent more than 20 years working in women’s cycling and creating opportunities for female athletes, so I feel strongly about protecting the integrity and fairness of the women’s category," Cranmer said.

"I believe eligibility should be determined by clear, consistent rules established by our sport’s governing bodies, particularly the UCI, and that those rules should be applied equally and transparently to every athlete.

"The UCI has established specific eligibility requirements for participation in the women’s category, and I believe those regulations need to be respected if athletes are to have confidence in the fairness of their competition.

MARTINA NAVRATILOVA SAYS BILLIE JEAN KING’S TRANS-ATHLETE STANCE ‘DOESN’T SQUARE’ WITH HER OWN WORDS

"For this individual to compete raises legitimate questions about whether the process was consistent with current UCI policy and how those eligibility requirements were interpreted and applied.

"Respecting individuals starts with respecting the female category. Every athlete deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, and women deserve a protected competitive category in which they can race fairly, safely and with confidence."

USA VOLLEYBALL SUGGESTS CHANGES COMING TO SEX TESTING, WHILE JUNIOR FAMILIES RAISE MALE ATHLETE CONCERNS

A race official who was there has provided a statement to OutKick addressing the situation.

"All riders were required to hold the appropriate international racing licenses, which officials cross-checked against UCI records before the event. Amanda Tait’s license and entry appeared valid, and nothing in the licensing information provided through USA Cycling identified Tait as male or otherwise indicated that Tait was ineligible to compete in the women’s field. 

"Race officials have also been repeatedly instructed that eligibility determinations of this kind are the responsibility of USA Cycling, not individual officials working registration or the race, even though clear eligibility requirements are defined in the UCI regs.

"The women’s race began at 8:35 Sunday morning. By the end of the first lap, officials’ phones began lighting up with messages from community members who recognized Tait on the broadcast and were questioning how Tait had been permitted to start in a UCI women’s race. 

"Officials identified Tait in the peloton, but Tait was subsequently dropped from the field and removed under the race’s standard time-cut procedures before any separate eligibility action could be taken. 

"Event staff and teams we spoke with after the race were unaware of the eligibility issue until it was brought to their attention. 


"From the information available to officials at registration, there was no apparent failure by the local registration team. The licensing information presented to them by USAC indicated that Tait was cleared to race in a women’s UCI event, and officials understood that eligibility decisions rested with USA Cycling."

The race was sanctioned by the UCI, while domestic licensing was handled by USA Cycling.

The trans athlete, Amanda Tait, has competed in more than 60 women’s events since entering the category, which was first reported by Reduxx.

Tait placed fourth at the USA Cycling Masters and Junior Road National Championships in June, pushing Olympic gold medalist Gwen Jorgensen out of the top five.

USA POWERLIFTING, ONCE IN TRANS ATHLETE LAWSUIT, SUPPORTS SCOTUS RULING: 'LAW HAS CAUGHT UP WITH THE SCIENCE'

Tait moved from USA Cycling’s women’s development category, which is designed for beginners, to pro-level competition, and rapidly ascended in as little as 18 months.

The male-born competitor won a women’s race at the Prospect Park Cycling Series in Brooklyn on Aug. 8.

Facing the trans athlete issue in their competitions, USA Cycling implemented new competition policy, which took effect in September 2025, but pro-life advocates have criticized its language as too weak to adequately protect the women’s division.

USA POWERLIFTING SETTLES TRANS ATHLETE DISCRIMINATION CASE BUT SAYS MINNESOTA IS 'OUT OF STEP' WITH SCIENCE

Their policy dictates, "Female means a person belonging, at conception, to the sex that produces the large reproductive cell." Eligibility for the women’s category is initially based on self-certification and an original birth certificate or other reliable facts, which critics say creates a loophole that can be exploited in states where sex markers can be amended.

The issue recalls the 2023 controversy over trans cyclist Austin Killips, whose dominant wins over female riders fueled concerns about fairness in women’s cycling.

USA Cycling retains sole authority to challenge a rider's category status, leaving female competitors, team staff and race marshals without an independent mechanism to contest eligibility on race day.

OutKick contacted USA Cycling's Bonnie Walker and the UCI for comment on their enforcement process, but received no response prior to publication.

item.title: ICE lodges detainer for illegal immigrant charged in wrong-way Maryland crash that killed mom, daughter
item.description: ICE lodged a detainer for Jose Antonio Caballero-Nolasco, an El Salvador immigrant charged with killing a mother and daughter in a wrong-way crash.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: An illegal immigrant from El Salvador charged with killing a mother and her daughter while driving drunk the wrong way on a Maryland freeway is being sought by federal immigration authorities.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has lodged a detainer request with authorities in Montgomery County for Jose Antonio Caballero-Nolasco, the Department of Homeland Security told Fox News Digital.

He is charged with two counts of grossly negligent manslaughter, two counts of homicide by motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol, and life-threatening injury by a motor vehicle.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED POLICE OFFICER AND HIS GIRLFRIEND

ILLEGAL ALIEN CHARGED WITH KILLING 4 YOUNG PEOPLE IN WRONG-WAY DUI CRASH ON OKLAHOMA HIGHWAY

Officials said Caballero-Nolasco was under the influence while driving the wrong way on Interstate 270 on Aug. 29, right before he crashed head-on into a vehicle with four people inside.

Two of the occupants, Musammat Shamima Begum, 46, and her 23-year-old daughter Areebah Jahin, were killed. They were from Northern Virginia and were on their way home at the time of the crash, affiliate FOX 5 D.C. reported.

Two others, a 62-year-old man and an 8-year-old girl, survived and were taken to local hospitals.

Investigators said they believe that alcohol impairment was a contributing factor in the crash.

ICE ARRESTS RELEASED ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF KILLING DAUGHTER, 9, IN ARIZONA ROLLOVER CRASH

"This tragedy was completely avoidable. Musammat Shamima Begum and Areebah Jahin should still be alive. ICE has lodged a detainer asking officials in Maryland to commit to not releasing this killer back onto our streets," said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. "My thoughts and prayers are with the victims and their family, and for a swift recovery for those who were injured."

Responding officers at the scene of the crash said Caballero-Nolasco smelled of alcohol, had bloodshot eyes, and slurred speech after the crash. He did not show any signs of braking before the crash, FOX 5 reported.

"There were some beer bottles that he admitted that he had been drinking," said Montgomery County State’s Attorney John McCarthy. "There were other bottles that were empty and full bottles were found within the vehicle."

Caballero-Nolasco was taken to a local hospital before being transferred to the Montgomery County Detention Center.

item.title: Rock concert at Virginia's Wolf Trap canceled after worker is crushed to death beneath tour bus
item.description: A tour bus support apparatus failed at Wolf Trap National Park, crushing a worker underneath, hours before Squeeze was set to perform Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
A rock performance at a venue in Virginia was canceled Thursday after a man working on a tour bus in a nearby parking lot was crushed underneath it hours before the show, according to authorities.

U.S. Park Police told FOX 5 DC they responded to the Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts at 5 p.m.

The English rock band "Squeeze" was scheduled to perform at 7:30 p.m. that night.

The worker was under the tour bus when officers arrived. Park Police said a supporting apparatus failed, causing the bus to come down on him.

CONNECTICUT DAD JUMPED TO HIS DEATH DURING CONCERT AT MADISON SQUARE GARDEN IN NYC: REPORT

"There was an accident involving a member of the community at Wolf Trap National Park," the venue said in a social media post. "Out of respect, tonight's show has been canceled."

"Squeeze are deeply saddened and shocked by an incident that occurred at the venue earlier today, which resulted in the loss of a life," the band said in a statement to Rolling Stone. "We will work with the promoter and venue regarding the possibility of rescheduling the show and will communicate further information to ticket holders as soon as it is available. Our thoughts remain with everyone affected by this tragic event."

COUNTRY STAR MARK CHESNUTT'S LONGTIME BANDMATE DIES UNEXPECTEDLY ON TOUR BUS

The worker's identity has not been released by Park Police.

News of the accident prompted some fans to leave, but many lingered in the parking lot, shaken by the death of the worker.

"It was horrible when we found out that happened," Debbie Daniel told FOX 5 DC. "We saw the emergency vehicles come in, figured something serious had happened because there was like 15 or more vehicles. But, yeah, it was very tragic."

Eric Anderson, another fan, empathized with the man's colleagues and agreed with the decision to cancel the show.

"Especially from what we're starting to understand about the circumstances, the show can't go on. And we understand that," Anderson said.

item.title: Pelosi, Omar join Trump and Schiff as unlikely alliance pushes to onshore key industry
item.description: Adam Schiff, Nancy Pelosi and Ilhan Omar back Donald Trump's federal film tax incentive to bring movie production back to California and America.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: President Donald Trump has gained several unlikely allies, including the man who led his first impeachment trial, in a major push to bring motion picture production back to California from other countries.

Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., who represented studio-heavy Burbank in Congress, was joined by Reps. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., in echoing support for Trump’s federal tax incentive plan to draw major film projects back to where it began.

"We’ve been promoting that for a long time. I’m glad he finally arrived at it," Pelosi told Fox News Digital when asked about the plan on the Capitol grounds.

PARAMOUNT ESCALATES THREAT TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA AS DEM AG'S ANTITRUST LAWSUIT STALLS WARNER BROS MERGER

Schiff tweeted earlier this week that he is "in strong agreement with the president."

The Democrat, who has accused Trump of colluding with Moscow to win the election and whom the president has responded to by calling him "pencil-neck," said it is time for Republicans and Democrats to "work together… get this done and bring the movie magic back to America."

SCHIFF ATTACK ON TRUMP’S DC INDYCAR RACE BACKFIRES AFTER DRIVER POINTS OUT CONTRADICTION

"Congress should immediately take up and pass a federal film tax incentive to bring back these good-paying jobs that we've lost to other countries."

Omar told Fox News Digital a similar refrain, adding that she has worked separately to attract film projects to Minneapolis.

FILM PRODUCER SAYS 'MADE IN AMERICA' MOVIES CAN HELP REVIVE HOLLYWOOD'S STRUGGLING INDUSTRY

She referenced "Fargo," the 1996 Coen Brothers comedy starring William H. Macy as an example of Minnesota’s ability to host large projects. The "Mighty Ducks" series starring Emilio Estevez and Joshua Jackson also filmed heavily in the Twin Cities during its 1990s run.

"When I was in the Minnesota House, I was very supportive of Minnesota having subsidies so we can have more movies being made inside Minnesota like the movie ‘Fargo’," she said.

She said the end of subsidies from St. Paul recently "made it less fun trying to run into people who were actually doing the production."

"It could be a really cool thing [and] also bring us money to states that can use it."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Trump appointed legendary actors Jon Voight, Mel Gibson and Sylvester Stallone special envoys to Hollywood. Gibson previously told Fox News that for a recent film, it was cheaper to fly the entire crew to Europe for three days than to shoot for one day in Los Angeles.

"There’s something really wrong there," he said, adding that another actor, ex-California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger, tried to assuage the problem while in office but was met with "obstacles."

Last year, another Trump foil also got on board with the idea of Washington bolstering Hollywood.

"California built the film industry – and we’re ready to bring even more jobs home… Now it’s time for a real federal partnership to Make America Film Again," said California Gov. Gavin Newsom.

Fox News Digital's Brie Stimson contributed to this report.

item.title: Rabbinic group accuses Jewish entertainers of 'whitewashing antisemitism' in Mark Ruffalo defense
item.description: The Coalition for Jewish Values accused over 170 Jewish entertainers of whitewashing antisemitism by defending Mark Ruffalo's merger criticism.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX — A rabbinic group is calling out some Jewish entertainers for "whitewashing antisemitism" by supporting actor Mark Ruffalo after his harsh opposition to the proposed Warner Bros. Discovery-Paramount merger.

More than 170 Jewish entertainers and artists signed a letter Tuesday "proudly" voicing support for Ruffalo after he was accused of antisemitism when criticizing the proposed $111 billion merger.

Coalition for Jewish Values, which represents over 2,500 traditional, Orthodox rabbis in American public policy, said it typically does not respond when a Hollywood figure says something it finds hateful about Jews or Israel. But the group believes Ruffalo’s comments forced a group of Jewish Hollywood figures that have "little knowledge of Jewish history or the nature of antisemitism" to "deny obvious bigotry."

MORE THAN 180 JEWISH ENTERTAINERS RALLY BEHIND ACTOR MARK RUFFALO IN PROTEST LETTER

"Ruffalo did not merely criticize a business deal. In an August 22 Instagram post tying the Paramount-Skydance/Warner Bros. merger to Oracle's work with Israel, Ruffalo claimed that the Ellison family — who are Jewish — were ‘powering some of the most destructive and inhuman forces in the world,’ and framed a corporate transaction as built on ‘genocide’ and ‘apartheid.’ That is not policy criticism, but mischaracterization of civil rights for Jews and Arabs as racism, and the rescue of Jewish hostages as murder," the Coalition for Jewish Values said in a statement.

"Nonetheless, more than 170 Jewish entertainment figures rushed to sign a letter dismissing the antisemitism charge as an ‘outrageous smear campaign.’ To be certain, they are entitled to their ignorant and misguided views," the statement continued. "They are not, however, entitled to be taken seriously when they engage in whitewashing antisemitism, or suggest that those with sufficient discernment to recognize the oldest of anti-Jewish tropes should deny the obvious."

The group said that "America set itself apart from much of the world precisely by declaring hatred of Jews unwelcome, regardless of who dressed it up as righteousness," and feels "Ruffalo would do well to remember that he owes much of his career to the Founding Fathers who made America so hospitable, and the Jews who fled persecution in Europe to build new homes for their children in a friendlier land."

JOHN CUSACK STANDS IN 'SOLIDARITY' WITH MARK RUFFALO AMID PARAMOUNT'S ANTISEMITISM ALLEGATION

"It is some of those children, working in New York in the early 20th century, who created Marvel Comics and invented The Incredible Hulk," the group said.

Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, told Fox News Digital that Ruffalo's remarks were "embarrassing" and that Ruffalo presented a "mythical inversion" of the situation in the Middle East.

Ruffalo was accused of invoking "antisemitic tropes" by Paramount after the Marvel star shared a video from August of Safra Catz, an Oracle executive vice chair and Paramount board member, discussing technology Oracle used to assist Israel after the Oct. 7 Hamas terrorist attack.

He linked Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, the father of Paramount CEO David Ellison, to financing behind the proposed acquisition and suggested the merger would be used to push "oppression."

"These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you," Ruffalo said. "Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle."

ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS

Among the Jewish artists who signed the letter were Abbi Jacobson, Alex Winter, Gina Gershon, Ilana Glazer, James Schamus, Joel Coen, Larry Charles, Kate Berlant, Naomi Klein, Sarah Sherman, Jane Schoenbrun, Todd Haynes and Tony Kushner, denied Ruffalo‘s comments were antisemitic, arguing that the executives Ruffalo criticized had "themselves have explicitly linked to their support for the ongoing depredations being visited on the people of Palestine and their silencing of critics of those horrors."

The celebrities also argued that a majority of American Jews now believe that Israel committed war crimes against Gaza, with a significant portion believing Israel is guilty of genocide. They called for an end to "spurious charges of antisemitism" against people like Ruffalo.

Ruffalo previously denied pushing antisemitism in a statement to Fox News Digital after Paramount's original condemnation.

"The accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest," Ruffalo said. "Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The proposed transaction would place CNN, HBO and Warner Bros. studio assets under the Ellison family’s control. A coalition of 12 state attorneys general sued to block it on antitrust grounds, and the companies agreed not to close until five days after a court ruling on the merits or June 1, 2027, whichever comes first.

Fox News Digital reached out to Ruffalo's representatives for additional comment.

Fox News Digital’s Lindsay Kornick and CJ Womack contributed to this report.

item.title: Fetterman faces Dem revolt as bombshell report fuels push to oust him: 'Disgrace'
item.description: Sen. Jon Fetterman's leaked texts reveal he dismissed meetings with Children's Hospital of Philadelphia over Medicaid cuts and skipped a police funeral.
item.content:encoded:
After a scathing report that called into question Sen. John Fetterman’s willingness to do the basic duties of a senator, some of his Democratic colleagues in Pennsylvania are eyeing ways to dislodge him from the upper chamber.

An explosive report from The Wall Street Journal painted Fetterman as a politician more interested in appearing on Fox News to discuss Israel than meeting with paralyzed veterans from his state, and blowing off a funeral for slain police officers because it would have taken too long.

And members of his own delegation are furious.

REPUBLICANS SAY THEY'D WELCOME FETTERMAN AS GOP EYES BIGGER SENATE MAJORITY

"There is a lot I could say about this report of John Fetterman’s pathetic behavior as a senator," Rep. Chris Deluzio, D-Pa., said on X. "But between the laziness, disrespect, and willingness to carry water for a foreign government, it shows us something we already know: this man has no sense of duty."

"He is not up for the high office he was elected to — and we in Pennsylvania will do something about it in 2028," he continued.

Behind the scenes, The Wall Street Journal’s report revealed through leaked text messages between Fetterman and his aides that the lawmaker was unwilling to do some of the core functions of the job, like meeting with constituents.

"John Fetterman is a disgrace," Rep. Brendan Boyle, D-Pa., said on X. "Our state deserves better than a lazy trust fund baby who is too lazy to do the job."

In one instance, Fetterman was told by an aide that representatives of the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) wanted to meet over concerns about Medicaid cuts. Fetterman asked why he had to keep meeting with CHOP, and the aide noted that they were worried about "vaccines and Medicaid cuts."

FETTERMAN UNDER FIRE AS GOV SHAPIRO PUSHES WILD CARD SENATOR TO 'GET BACK' TO BEING A DEMOCRAT

"Well, I’m not," Fetterman responded. "I’m convinced they just want free trips to D.C."

Another instance came when an aide told Fetterman that there would be a dress code at a funeral for three police officers killed in Pennsylvania last year, and that the service was expected to last for three hours.

"This may be a nonstarter," Fetterman wrote.

Years before his time in the Senate, Fetterman rose to prominence as a progressive who appeared to emulate the formula laid out by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., who he backed early on in his runs for the White House.

When Fetterman won his seat in 2022 against Dr. Mehmet Oz, who now runs the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Fetterman ran on a platform of universal healthcare, pro-labor policies and higher tax rates on wealthy Americans — key hallmarks of progressive politics.

Since ascending to the Senate, however, his voting record has shown a more moderate flair, and questions are swirling over whether he will jump ship and join the GOP. He’s bucked his party on several occasions since taking office, too.

DNC VICE CHAIR ATTACKS DEMOCRATIC SEN. JOHN FETTERMAN: 'YOU’RE A MESS'

During the government shutdown fight last year, he joined Republicans as Democrats stayed unified in their push to renew lapsing Obamacare tax credits, has become one of the most vocal proponents of Israel, and helped to confirm some of President Donald Trump’s nominees, including Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin — notably, he voted against his old political rival Oz.

The desire to boot Fetterman extends beyond just his colleagues in the Pennsylvania congressional delegation.

Pennsylvania state Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta, who is the vice chair of the Democratic National Committee, has his sights set on Fetterman, too.

"This report is horrifying, but not new to many of us in PA. John barely showed up as [Lieutenant Governor] and is constantly MIA as our senator," Kenyatta said on X.

"When he’s not on FOX cheerleading Trump & endless wars, he is attacking the very neighbors who gave him a chance," he continued. "2028 can’t come soon enough."

Fetterman did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Here's what the NFL should put in the end zone instead of "End Racism"
item.description: The NFL's "End Racism" end zone messaging returns for 2026, but fatherlessness, abortion rates and hunger in the Black community need attention.
item.content:encoded:
In case you missed it, the NFL will once again put "End Racism" & "Stop Hate" in the end zones, as well as allow social justice messages on helmets for the 2026 season. It's clearly virtue signaling that does nothing of substance. It was objectively a knee-jerk reaction to the woke wave of 2020. Instead of virtue signaling with statements about racism in a league that is predominately Black, I have a few "social justice" messages that would actually make a positive impact.

Before I share my suggestions, let me take you back to 2020.

The NFL first introduced "End Racism" in its end zones in 2020, following the nationwide race riots and destructive protests after the death of George Floyd and growing pressure from NFL players. On July 27, 2020, the league told teams that "End Racism" and "It Takes All of Us" would be stenciled in opposite end zones during Week 1 and home openers. They obviously framed the death of Floyd as racism and went along with a narrative that America and its police force, many of which helped keep teams and fans safe at every stadium around the country throughout the season, are racist. The NFL said the initiative was designed to show "how football and the NFL brings people together to work as one and use our example and our actions to help conquer racism." There you have it. They explained without a doubt that they believe racism is a major issue and it must be "conquered" through messaging in the end zones. I'm chuckling writing this.

NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS

Commissioner Roger Goodell subsequently confirmed that the social justice messaging was part of the league’s "Inspire Change" program, which was developed in consultation with players and the NFL Players Association. The move came shortly after Goodell acknowledged that the NFL had been "wrong" for not listening to players earlier regarding racism.

One of the best responses to all of this was from Barstool's PFT Commentator, who said, "I used to be racist as f--- until the NFL painted "End Racism" in the end zone." That was the perfect way to expose the nonsensical nature of the initiative. It was divisive and eye-roll inducing. The fact the league is still pushing this messaging is laughable, but if they really wanted to tackle issues facing our nation and the black community, here are a few messaging suggestions to replace "End Racism":

Fatherlessness is an epidemic. There is a large number of children growing up without their biological father living in the home, and research consistently links the absence of a father in the home with disadvantages in education, behavior, economic stability and later-life outcomes. The NFL should lean into this because the issue is particularly pronounced among Black Americans.

A Congressional Research Service report found that 64% of African-American children lived apart from their biological fathers in 2012, compared with about one-third of children overall. Research on the Fragile Families data found that 51% of African-American fathers in the study had been incarcerated by the time their child was five, and children whose fathers had been incarcerated showed significantly more behavioral problems. These disadvantages can carry into school and eventually the workforce: studies have found paternal incarceration is associated with lower school readiness and educational outcomes, while research by American economist Raj Chetty and colleagues found that Black boys who grow up in communities with greater Black father presence have higher employment rates and are less likely to be incarcerated as adults. There are other factors that effect children in these communities, but the evidence suggests that having an involved father can be an important protective factor that improves a child's chances of succeeding academically, economically and socially. It would be an initiative the NFL could lean into that could have a positive impact in a tangible way.

WHAT MY SON'S ULTRASOUND TAUGHT ME ABOUT ABORTION — AND MASSACHUSETTS IGNORES

There is no denying that abortion is a very emotional, highly debated topic in America. It's undoubtedly been an issue that has effected the black community more than any other in America. Since 2020, stats show an estimated 4+ million abortions have occurred from 2020 through 2023, according to the Guttmacher Institute. Again, the issue is particularly significant in the Black community: in 2022, Black women accounted for 39.5% of reported abortions despite representing a much smaller percentage of women of reproductive age, and their abortion rate of 24.4 per 1,000 women was 4.3 times the rate for White women (5.7 per 1,000).

The NFL was so upset and bent out of shape by the death of George Floyd that they made a definitive stance against unjustified deaths, so how about standing up against the injustice of child death, NFL? You could help save millions of innocent lives if you made an effort to provide resources, curriculum, and dove head first into community outreach in this area.

COLIN KAEPERNICK IS RIGHT ABOUT THE NFL'S 'PERFORMATIVE' RACISM CAMPAIGN — BUT HE'S ALSO A HYPOCRITE

Hunger is a major issue in Black communities in the United States, with 9.2 million Black Americans experiencing food insecurity in 2023—about 22.4% of the Black population, compared with 10.4% of non-Hispanic White Americans. Black children are especially vulnerable: 27% lived in food-insecure households, meaning roughly 1 in 4 Black children did not have consistent access to enough food. Hunger can obviously affect a child’s health, concentration, academic performance and long-term development.

The NFL is uniquely positioned to help because of its enormous reach and resources in many of the communities most affected. The league could expand its existing community programs by partnering with food banks, funding mobile food pantries, providing meals to children during the offseason and directing team charitable dollars toward local food-security programs.

The NFL already has a framework for this through Inspire Change, which has directed more than $375 million toward social-justice and community organizations, including programs focused on economic advancement and opportunity. If the NFL wants to make a tangible difference in Black communities, fighting hunger is one area where its money, visibility and local team infrastructure could produce an immediate and measurable impact.

The NFL has the ability to actually do something of value, not just virtue signal after the death a Black man that was politicized to make people believe police officers were hunting black folks, America was foundationally racist, and racism was more than just a fringe issue causing institutional harm to the black community.

item.title: Miami opens its post-Carson Beck era against Stanford in a key college football week 1 matchup
item.description: Miami Hurricanes open their season with just eight returning starters and new quarterback Darian Mensah facing a Stanford team already warmed up.
item.content:encoded:
Can you believe we are already here? Friday of Week 1 of College Football. Do you even know what is on the horizon for us? Tonight, there are a handful of games, after we had a decent slate yesterday. Tomorrow, a full day of the gridiron commences. Then, the NFL comes next week, and we are on the verge of having football every week until basically February. I. Can’t. Wait.

item.title: Fake patient portal scam can steal your login and infect your PC
item.description: MyChart phishing emails mimic real patient portal alerts with fake lab results and malware tricks that target Windows users across the country.
item.content:encoded:
If you have ever checked a lab result or sent your doctor a message online, you may already know MyChart. It is a widely used patient portal from Epic that hospitals and medical practices use to give patients online access to health information and care teams.

That growing reliance on patient portals caught the attention of Mary M. She recently wrote to us after hearing from her primary care physician, or PCP, and several specialists about moving more of their patient communication online.

"I just got a lot of updates from my PCP and specialist doctors saying they are moving toward this, but they are already compromised!! I think this is a topic for you!"

Mary raised a concern many patients may share as they hear about scams targeting MyChart users. There is an important point to clear up. The warnings reviewed here describe criminals impersonating MyChart through phishing campaigns. They do not report a breach of the MyChart platform itself.

MEDICARE AND SOCIAL SECURITY SCAMS: WARNING SIGNS AND TIPS

Epic has documented scams that copy the MyChart experience to steal login details. One version can also push malware onto Windows computers. Here's how the scam works and how to protect yourself before a fake MyChart alert catches you off guard.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com

This one caught my attention because the warnings are coming from several credible sources at nearly the same time. Penn Medicine said on Aug. 26, 2026, that it was seeing a nationwide scam involving emails and text messages made to look like they came from MyChart. Then, on Aug. 28, Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday warned consumers about another MyChart impersonation scam involving a bogus Medicare Kit.

Epic has also detailed two phishing campaigns its security team investigated this summer. Put all of that together, and you can see why I want you to be especially careful with unexpected MyChart messages right now.

The tricky part is that many of us are already used to getting legitimate emails about appointments or new test results. A fake MyChart alert can land right alongside the real ones, and scammers are counting on you reacting before you take a closer look.

One campaign starts with a message that looks routine. Epic says the email carries MyChart branding and tells the recipient, "Your recent results are ready."

The button inside the email leads to a fake sign-in page. According to Epic, scammers copied code from the real MyChart site, which helps the page look convincing.

The bogus page asks for an email address and password. If you enter them, the scammers can capture those credentials. Then the attack gets more aggressive.

After the victim signs in, the fake site displays a made-up medical record. Epic says one version shows a pop-up claiming an "AI-powered review" found critical patterns in blood work.

That is a powerful pressure tactic. A warning about your health can be much harder to ignore than an ordinary phishing message.

Epic says real critical results come from your care team rather than a website pop-up. The fake chart then claims you need to complete a human verification step before seeing more information.

This part should stop you immediately. Epic says the site instructs Windows users to press the Windows key and R, paste content from the clipboard and press Enter. Those steps open the Windows Run box and execute a command the website placed on the clipboard. According to Epic, following those instructions installs malware.

Epic also saw an August 2026 version with an "Unlock Full Report & See Diagnosis" button. Clicking it downloaded a Windows file called Full_Analysis_Report.exe. The page then coached the victim through bypassing the computer's security warning. Your medical results should appear inside MyChart. A patient portal should never require you to download a Windows program to reveal a diagnosis.

FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK

The second campaign uses a different hook. Epic says scammers sent fake emails telling people they had been selected for a "2026 Medicare Health Kit." Penn Medicine has also warned about messages advertising a free "MyChart Medicare Kit" or "Senior Health Package." MyChart does not run giveaways.

After someone clicks, Epic says the link can pass through unrelated advertising sites before reaching a fake MyChart-branded survey. A countdown clock pushes the victim to move quickly. Eventually, the site says the kit costs $0 but asks for a shipping fee. Before payment, it collects personal information. The final page asks for credit card details. Epic says no kit ships.

Patients already expect electronic messages from doctors and hospitals. A real test-result notification may show up on the same day as a fake one. Scammers can copy that familiar routine. They can also use fear to shorten the amount of time you spend checking a message.

If a fake portal hints at a serious health problem, your first instinct may be to find out what happened. That is why opening the portal independently can make such a difference. We recently covered another healthcare scam that uses fake QR codes around medical settings. Those codes can send patients to bogus sites asking for patient portal credentials or Medicare information. The MyChart campaign follows the same basic idea. The scammer borrows trust from a healthcare service you already recognize.

A few simple steps can help you slow things down before an urgent-looking message leads you to the wrong place.

If an email says a new result is waiting, avoid using the button inside the message. Open the MyChart app directly. You can also use a saved bookmark or start from your healthcare provider's official website. Epic says each healthcare organization can have its own MyChart URL. You can use MyChart.org to find your provider's official portal.

Do not rely on the sender name alone. An email can display "MyChart" while coming from an unrelated address. Look at the full address and compare it with previous legitimate messages from your healthcare provider. If anything feels off, contact your provider through a phone number or website you already trust.

MyChart says it will never tell you to use keyboard shortcuts or run a command to verify, fix or unlock your account. A website asking you to open the Windows Run box should be an immediate warning sign. Close the page.

MyChart supports two-step verification (2FA). The extra check can help protect your account if someone gets your password. Depending on your setup, you can verify your login through a code or an authenticator app. MyChart also supports passkeys, which can reduce your reliance on a reusable password.

Avoid reusing a password from another important account. A password manager can create and store a strong password for you. If a phishing site captures one password, reuse can turn one stolen login into a much larger problem.

The malware part of this scam shows why strong security protection still has a role. Strong antivirus software can help warn you about malicious downloads or suspicious websites.
